name: Buffalo Bill State Park (Lake Shore Campground)
note: Lake Shore Campground (formerly North Shore Bay), about 9 mi W of Cody on US-14/16/20 between the highway and Buffalo Bill Reservoir: three small paved loops on sagebrush points above the north shore, a short walk down to the water. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API, PlaceId 7 'Buffalo Bill State Park', FacilityId 309 'Lake Shore', read 2026-11-20): 36 web-bookable units - 22 'Campsite Electric' (LS-01..21, LS-23; 20/30/50 A), 9 'Campsite Non-Electric' (LS-24..32), 5 drive-in tent sites T-01..T-05; every RV site 'Site Access: Drive-In', paved pads 'Unit & Parking Size(ft)' 30-90 (13 pull-throughs) -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. Not in the DB: the only Buffalo Bill SP entry is 6349 North Fork, 8.6 km W; nothing else within 8 km. Public: no price gate. Corroborated by The Dyrt (Lake Shore Campground, 7 reviews 4.3/5, latest 2026-09-05) and the park page capture (2026-10-12) naming Lake Shore as open in winter.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery at 44.5007,-109.2335 (900 m) and the W/mid/E loops at 220-260 m frames, every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (MapInfo lat/lng, FacilityId 309) plotted; images rendered. The three loops sit on sagebrush points between US-14/16/20 and the reservoir; south of the pads lies ~25-40 m of sage slope with scattered trees and footpaths, then a wide bare drawdown/wave-washed band to water well below full pool. Full pool = top of active conservation 5,393.5 ft (~1643.9 m; Reclamation/Powell Tribune). USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar (epqs.nationalmap.gov) profiles from the pads toward the water (lidar water surface 1642.8 m): sites 12 ~55-60 m, 14 ~60-65 m, 16 ~70-75 m, 25 ~65-70 m, 27 ~60-65 m, 29 ~65-70 m, 04 ~70 m to the full-pool contour, each descending 7-9 m; site 06 is ~30-35 m from it but atop a cutbank (1650.9 m -> 1647.6 m in 5 m, then 1644.8 m at 30 m: a climb-down). Every RV pad lies beyond the ~50 m bound or above a steep bank -> open lake view, not lakefront. The booking site's 'Waterfront Setting: Reservoir' tag on LS-08..32 and T-01..05 is generous (measured, not the basis). A Dyrt reviewer (2026-09-05): 'Above the lake but with some short hike can get to shoreline.'

fees.note: $10 a night for Wyoming residents, $18 for others, +$10 at an electric site, plus the day-use fee, $7 a vehicle for residents and $12 for others, plus sales and lodging tax. The booking site shows 'Fees Range From $33-50 (Per Night, Per 1 Vehicle)' on the electric sites and '$23-40' on the non-electric ones.

season_source: audit/state_park_fees/wy_pages_2026-10-12.json capture of https://wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/places-to-go/buffalo-bill (read 2026-10-12): 'Park is open year round for camping and day use.' ... 'October - April: North Fork Campground Closed; Stagecoach Campground Closed; Sheep Mountain Day Use Area Closed; Rest of park open to camping and day use, ALL water systems turned off for the winter season.' reserve.wyoming.gov sells Lake Shore nights from May 1 (search/place InSeason false 2027-04-30, true 2027-05-01 .. 2027-10-15; read 2026-11-20).

booking.note: All 36 sites are bookable online from May 1; the campground stays open in winter (water off), outside the booking season.

booking_source: reserve.wyoming.gov US eDirect API FacilityId 309: AllowWebBooking true on all 36 units; Restrictions MaximumStay 14, MinimumStay 1; InSeason from 2027-05-01 (false 2027-04-30), read 2026-11-20.
flags: Lake Shore is the old North Shore Bay Campground renamed (search snippets of the park's own pages: 'Lake Shore Bay Campground has 37 sites', 'Lake Shore Campground located 9 miles west of Cody on 14/16/20'; Hipcamp and a Cody tourism listing still use 'North Shore Bay', 37 sites). North Shore Bay is therefore NOT a separate missing campground. reserve.wyoming.gov PlaceId 7 has only two campgrounds (309 Lake Shore, 310 North Fork = 6349) plus day-use shelters, Shreve Lodge, Stagecoach camp shacks (313) and the Trout Creek group site.

Waterfront downgraded to lakeview from the booking site's 'Waterfront Setting: Reservoir' tag: 3DEP lidar puts the RV pads 55-75 m and 7-9 m above the full-pool line (site 06 ~30-35 m but atop a steep cutbank). Close to the 50 m bound at sites 12/14 if the Reclamation full-pool datum sits ~1 m above lidar - reviewer may want to look.

Showers and dump station left unsourced: a 2024 Campendium review (search snippet only; campendium refuses) says pit toilets and no showers; Dyrt reviews disagree on whether the dump station is in this campground.
